## Queen of the Nile

From my entire _Egyptian Turquoise_ series, the "Queen of the Nile" has easily been my most popular (and most stolen) piece of art. I worked with Arike on multiple pieces from this series, who in all openness was insanely patient with our indecisive asses as we discussed angles, makeup, and even some work with projection art.

The most famous shot with Arike is the one here on the right, which was originally posted [here on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B5JAuF4lh6n/). It quickly became the most popular and in fact the centerpiece of the entire series... the "face of the series" (pun intended). At almost every single art show that I put on, you'll find at least one version of "Queen of the Nile" among the prints. In fact, if I remember right, I only left her out of a single show. And at THAT show, it was the number one question asked: _"Where's the queen?"_

It's a mistake I only had to learn once.

**Full Credits**:

content.text:
## Egyptian Turquoise: Series + History

My friend Duane ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/hopifilmmaker/)) has introduced me to even more incredible Hopi history than I'd known before. Stay with me, btw... it connects. Well, that and he also got me in to go see "The Return of the Force" ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/thereturnoftheforce/)) feature gallery while it was still in Durango, Colorado. One of the things he taught me was that Anasazi was not some ancient, dead tribe of the southwest... it was a name used by the Navajo to describe the Hopi, and in ways, to insult them. The word translates literally to "enemy" btw. It's an awesome name. But when you hear Anasazi, know that they're talking about the Hope tribe of the cliffs and mesas of the US Southwest. Yeah, the same tribe that basically predicted the past 150-years right up to the internet itself. That's them.

We'll get to connecting the dots in a second... but first, let's spray a little more loose paint on the canvas in a different area. This time blue paint.

_Because blue didn't exist._

If you don't know how words and definitions impact our perception and internal construction of the world around us, then let it be said that the color "blue" has been lost and found multiple times throughout history and has only recently been re-discovered. The Hopi (Anasazi) had been mining turquoise and malachite 2,000-years ago and _they_ knew the color blue. They've always had a diverse and descriptive language.

But it was Ancient Egypt to be the first in all of history to have words for "blue" and "turquoise", using them in their art and culture... praising them... worshipping them. They even understood the math connected to each color. Their priests attributed colors to music, connecting them to song itself. There along the banks of The River Nile, these priests forged a history upon papyrus that time itself could not fade nor tear asunder.

The _Egyptian Turquoise_ series is my honoring of that incredible legacy.

Note: This portrait of Arike here on the right is with the same exact crew, but from an entirely different shoot, with completely different makeup and my "[Bangles del Aguila](bangles-del-aguila)" fractal more clear throughout it.

## Egyptian Turquoise: TINY BLVCK

I love Arike, she's my bud! And again, she was so patient with us on these shoots. But Ayinde? _Ayinde's my fucking queen!_

While "Queen of the Nile" with Arike (aka, "TINY BLVCK") is the big hit of the series, none of this would've ever happened if Tiny and I hadn't met on the playa at Burning Man. None of it. Huddling around the fire together for warmth, I told the story that Flip Solomon ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/flipsolomon/)) had once told to me... and that she in turn had heard from a Ted Talk.

_<font face="Times New Roman">When the math legend Ron Eglash journeyed to the Ba-ila village in southern Zambia, he walked up to the chief with a pretty strange request: "Can I stand on your roof?" What Eglash had spotted from above was a fractal pattern -- not just in the architecture, but woven into the entire layout of the village. Those exact same intricate geometric patterns were mirrored in their makeup, their clothing, even their hairstyles. The Ba-ila weren't surprised. To them, it was entirely natural to iterate and build on the patterns that held the deepest meaning. You can find these tribal fractals echoing all across the continent.</font>_

Out there in the dust, Tiny and I turned into a veritable storm of creativity. We spent hours talking over ideas for fractal fashion, mapping out different shoots, and geeking out over how tribal makeup tied directly back to those native fractals. Since I spend my days weaving intricate patterns into my own works, it was a perfect collision of worlds. She already had a makeup artist on lock and friends deep in the industry. The second I told her about the history of turquoise tracing all the way back to Ancient Egypt... it was basically over. It _had_ to happen.

While "The Mesmer" (on right) is one of the pieces I crafted with and of Ayinde, I named the piece below after the series itself... exactly like a title track on an album. It had to be TINY BLVCK to take top billing for me. Hands down, it's my personal favorite from the entire run.

Ayinde started a family just a few months before the pandemic hit. Then, about a year deep into the plague, she nixed her Instagram and went scorched earth on all her sites. You can still find links to her pages floating around out there... they just lead to dead ends. I still hold out hope that I'll cross paths with her at the burn again one day. We never did get around to fully launching that fashion line-up idea... but I haven't given up on it... and I definitely haven't stopped working on it.

_One day, it'll happen._

**Full Credits**:

*   Design, Fractals, Processing: **San Jaya Prime**
*   Modeling, Hair: **TINY BLVCK** (aka, "**Ayinde**")
*   Make-Up: **Orente Unlimited**
*   Photography: **ImageSense Media**
*   Available On: **[Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/40607160)**

content.caption: "Bangles of Ayinde" -- Unfinished draft, even years later, and at this point I'm thinking I'll need to construct the dome itself in Blender then render the fractal over the dome itself. Ayinde's design and portrait are almost perfect at this point, maybe just a bit more coloring and potential lighting adjustments once the fractal dome itself is finished... lol, in like 15-more years. You know what? No! Fuck that shit! I'm hiring as of right now. Anyone who reads this and thinks they've got the skills in Blender to render a dome, lit from around the inner circle of it at the bottom, and with my fractal mapped to it, [contact me](contact). Smash that contact button and send me a line. Let me know your price and thoughts. _Bring it on!_

content.text:
## Egyptian Turquoise: iMeenaTV

Thank YOU Amina! Finally, at least my Aries sister still has at least one profile still up and running ([iMeenaTV on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/imeenatv/)). I got two thirds through this entry and thought I wasn't going to be able to link to anyone. _I owe you a coffee next time we jam out together woman!_

At the time of our first shoots, Meena really was the baby of the group. I swear though that she must grow backwards in time, because whenever we send each other a line, 1000% she looks younger and younger. Weirdest fucking thing ever! Amina's not only a fellow Aries and mischief maker, but she's also one heck of a coder. Straight up hammer! In fact, it's Meena who turned me on to the organization Black Girls Code. Marvel might've somehow yoinked the character and brain of Shuri from this woman right here -- iMeenaTV.

We worked with the same crew for the shoot, but wanted to create a geometric form of hypnotism in the final piece. Thus... _The Curioso_ was born. Using a series of fractal feathers as the backdrop, then a few different triangles formed from optical illusions in the foreground, it was Orente who made the call to match up some of the makeup with what we were planning with the geometry.

**Full Credits**:

*   Design, Fractals, Processing: **San Jaya Prime**
*   Modeling, Hair: **Amina Ismaila** (aka, "**iMeenaTV**"; aka, "**Meena**")
*   Make-Up: **Orente Unlimited**
*   Photography: **ImageSense Media**
*   Available On: [**Instagram Only**](https://www.instagram.com/p/B5iKmaulc9F/)

## The Curioso

**Fun Fact #1**: Meena wanted to wear green contacts for the shoot. Orente shot it down. I was never quite certain about the call, so during processing I called Amina over... asking her if she saw anything she liked and had to keep.. . or that she didn't like and wanted to have edited. She looked, then looked again, and said, "Change nothing." She was smiling as she walked away.

**Fun Fact #2**: None of the final pieces with Amina are on Redbubble. She was 17 at the time of the shoot and securing licensing for sales would need to be cleared (again) with both of her parents. I uh... lol, I could do without meeting her mother a second time. Meena you know I'm right! Besides, I like that there are a few that aren't up for sale.

**Fun Fact #3**: For this current version of _The Curioso_ here on the right, Ameena herself coded the script to create the triangle. I told her the challenge was to create a triangle that defies 3D laws to form an illusion. She went a step further and programmed three different illusions inside of it.

### Egyptian Turquoise: Retrospective

The series isn't over. I have other pieces from the series where I worked with other artists. Some are even on Instagram. I already had a few sketches down on paper before seeing the "Arcane" series ([Netflix](https://www.netflix.com/title/81435684)), where Mel and Ambessa Medarda threw me into a renewed fit of creativity. Especially on the fashion side, as Tiny was right... we really need to work textiles and more organic additions like bone, then Egyptian treasures like jade... ah, there's so much more to explore here.

I'm set to retire here in a few years and get back to the art world full time.

You can be damned sure this will be a part of it.

## In Love + Gratitude

To our queens, my love and gratitude. Arike, Meena, fucking Ayinde! You'll always be _my queen_, Tiny. May every horizon open before your feet and the waves rise at your command. To Orente and iSense, my feeble halfwit mind doesn't comprehend an iota of what you do and how you accomplish it. I just stand back slack-jawed in awe of your incredible work and wish I had the words to describe it. Tiny? Tiny has words for that. Mad shout out in gratitude to both of you. _Seriously!_

I did in fact leave a bit of the story out... a bit further back. . but I'm not closing it out yet.

I cannot put into words how much it means to me that Mario of the Jicarilla Apache not only took me in, but then taught me how to work with silver and turquoise. Those months instilled in me an appreciation of the craft and colors themselves that has never faded, and in fact has only growth in strength over time. Then years later, Zero's grand daddy Pops (aka, "Walt Rambo") showed me even more ways to work with silver and other metals. What you see here in my 2D arts and works are because of these incredible creatures who shared with me the secrets of their crafts and took the time to reveal the inner workings of their wizardry. I'm forever indebted to you all. _Thank you. Truly._

A huge shout out in thanks to Duane of Hopi, who's taken what small knowledge I had of "the people of the mesa" and cracked that wide open, no matter whether talking about lore while enjoying a meal together, or talking about the way the land has differed over the past millennia and how the tribes once worked _with_ and traversed the lands... all while out hiking in the perfect setting. Anyone who hasn't really taken a moment to sink their teeth into both Arizona and New Mexico just doesn't understand what turquoise and these colors really mean.

And I said it before, and I'll say it again. My love and gratitude to _you_, Tiny... sitting around that fire at Burning Man and talking about the ancient worlds. . how even time and space melts away and dissolves when the whole of history comes together... when the pattern is revealed. _Nights like that should last forever._
